# 2 Samuel Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 192v–192r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_020_page_001.jpg, 2SA_020_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Now a troublemaker named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite, happened to be there. He sounded the ram's horn and shouted, "We have no stake in David! We owe nothing to the son of Jesse! Everyone go home, Israel!"

**2** So all the men of Israel deserted David and followed Sheba son of Bichri. But the men of Judah stayed loyal to their king all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

**3** When David arrived at his palace in Jerusalem, he took the ten concubines he had left to look after the house and placed them in a guarded residence. He provided for their needs but never slept with them again. They lived there in confinement, like widows, for the rest of their lives.

**4** The king ordered Amasa, "Mobilize the men of Judah and report back to me within three days."

**5** Amasa went out to mobilize Judah, but he took longer than the deadline the king had set.

**6** David said to Abishai, "Sheba son of Bichri is going to cause us more trouble than Absalom ever did. Take my men and go after him before he reaches fortified cities and slips through our fingers."

**7** So Joab's men marched out, along with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the elite warriors. They left Jerusalem in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.

**8** When they reached the great stone at Gibeon, Amasa came out to meet them. Joab was wearing his military tunic with a sword strapped over it in a sheath at his hip. As he stepped forward, the sword slid out.

**9** Joab said to Amasa, "How are you, brother?" and with his right hand he grabbed Amasa's beard as if to kiss him.

**10** Amasa never saw the sword in Joab's other hand. Joab plunged it into his belly, and his intestines spilled out onto the ground. One thrust was all it took — Amasa was dead. Then Joab and his brother Abishai continued the pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.

**11** One of Joab's men stood over Amasa's body and called out, "If you're for Joab and if you're for David — follow Joab!"

**12** But Amasa was lying in a pool of blood in the middle of the road, and every soldier who came along stopped to stare. When the man realized the body was holding everyone up, he dragged Amasa off the road into a field and threw a cloth over him.

**13** Once the body was out of sight, everyone moved on and followed Joab in pursuit of Sheba son of Bichri.

**14** Sheba traveled through all the tribes of Israel until he reached Abel Beth-maacah. All the Bicrites rallied to him and followed him into the city.

**15** Joab's forces arrived and laid siege to Abel Beth-maacah. They built a siege ramp against the outer wall, and the troops began battering the wall to bring it down.

**16** Then a wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab to come over here — I need to speak with him!"

**17** When he approached, the woman asked, "Are you Joab?" He said, "I am." She said, "Hear what your servant has to say." He replied, "I'm listening."

**18** She said, "There's an old saying: 'Go ask at Abel,' and that would settle the matter.

**19** I represent a city that is peaceful and loyal in Israel. You are trying to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why would you swallow up what belongs to the LORD?"

**20** Joab answered, "Never! I would never swallow up or destroy!

**21** That's not what this is about. A man from the hill country of Ephraim — Sheba son of Bichri — has rebelled against King David. Hand him over, just him, and I will pull back from the city." The woman told Joab, "His head will be thrown over the wall to you."

**22** The woman went to the people of the city with her plan. They cut off Sheba's head and tossed it to Joab. He sounded the ram's horn, and the troops dispersed from the city and went home. Joab returned to the king in Jerusalem.

**23** Joab commanded the entire army of Israel. Benaiah son of Jehoiada commanded the Cherethites and Pelethites.

**24** Adoram was in charge of forced labor. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the royal recorder.

**25** Sheva was the court secretary. Zadok and Abiathar were priests.

**26** And Ira the Jairite served as David's personal priest.

---
*— PNEUMA*
